text: Part of the chicken's respiratory tract is similar to other animals: the glottis is the start of the tract and closes when feed passes down the throat so it does not enter the lungs; the trachea is made of cartilaginous rings and divides into two smaller tubes called bronchi; the lungs are relatively small, do not expand, and are firmly attached to the ribs. One part is specific to birds: air passes through the lungs by means of 9 air sacs — balloon-like structures with thin, transparent membranes at the ends of the airway system. The air sacs extend into pneumatic bones such as the humerus.
